intro: Hi, I'm Dumplings Majesty — born in China, currently based in Tokyo, working on AI and enterprise systems in Japan.
My career spans DXC, Microsoft, IBM, and FITEC, where I've worked extensively on cloud platforms, automation systems, and the design and delivery of enterprise applications.
I hold a master's degree and focus on machine learning, deep learning, and applied AI engineering.

Over the years I've worked on smart office systems, manufacturing information systems, AI-based visual inspection, and cross-platform app development — all of which sharpened my focus on how technology creates real business value. Outside of work, I enjoy traveling and diving.

intro: I go by "Dumplings Majesty" — obviously not my real name, just because I love eating dumplings. As a student I knew nothing about Python, Machine Learning, or AI, so after starting work I began a long journey of self-study. I really appreciated all the people online quietly sharing what they'd learned, and it helped me a lot — so I decided to do the same and give back what I've learned.

I'm assuming you already have some basic Python knowledge, and that you're someone who gets stuck in daily work not knowing what a certain function does. Here I first summarize how to use various NumPy and Pandas functions, and later I'll also summarize the pitfalls I ran into while tinkering with things like scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and MXNet. Hope it helps.
There are definitely mistakes, and it's definitely not complete — but anyway, growth is all about making mistakes along the way.
NumPy → Pandas → Machine Learning — that's my path of self-improvement...

intro: My kid is learning Japanese kanji, and we often use kanji practice worksheet PDFs from sites like print-kids.net — a single page can have dozens of PDF links, and clicking through and downloading them one by one got tedious, so I wrote a small tool that grabs every PDF linked from a given practice page in one go.

The link-finding part walks a, iframe, embed, and object tags on the page and collects any whose href/src/data attribute points to a .pdf file. For links a script generated dynamically that aren't caught by a tag attribute, it falls back to scanning the raw HTML with a regex so fewer links slip through.

Each filename is built primarily from the visible label text next to the link (stripping the trailing "ダウンロード" that commonly appears), falling back to the title attribute, and finally to the filename from the URL path if neither is available. The generated name is then sanitized to strip out characters the filesystem won't allow, so saving never fails on a bad character.

Downloads are streamed to disk in chunks rather than loading a whole file into memory at once. If a file with the same name already exists it's skipped automatically, so re-running the script never re-downloads anything and an interrupted run can just be resumed; it also prints progress ("N of M") as it goes.

The default target page is a 2nd-grade kanji review sheet, but you can pass any other print-kids.net practice page URL as a command-line argument, so it's easy to reuse for different grades or topics — I've already used it to pull down over 280 practice PDFs and print them out for my kid.
topics: Automatically extracts PDF links by scanning the href/src/data attributes of a, iframe, embed, and object tags on the target page
Falls back to a regex scan of the raw HTML to catch script-generated links the tag parser misses
Builds filenames from the link's visible text (stripping a trailing "ダウンロード"), falling back to the title attribute and then the URL path's filename
Sanitizes generated filenames, stripping characters the filesystem doesn't allow
Skips files that were already downloaded, so re-runs and resumed downloads never duplicate work
Streams downloads to disk in chunks and prints progress ("N of M") as it runs
Accepts any print-kids.net practice page URL via a command-line argument, not just the default 2nd-grade kanji page
Reuses a requests.Session when fetching the target page, with SSL certificate verification issues worked around for local environments

usage.title: Usage
steps: Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt (requires requests and beautifulsoup4)
Run python download_kanji_pdfs.py directly to download every PDF from the default page (a 2nd-grade kanji review sheet)
To download a different grade or topic, pass the target page URL as an argument, e.g.: python download_kanji_pdfs.py https://print-kids.net/print/kokugo/1nensei-kanji1/
Downloaded PDFs are saved to the downloads/ folder; progress is printed as it runs, and re-running the script never re-downloads files that already exist
